annotator.caution: Every value is a first-pass reading of the reference text and needs human review before it is used as evaluation ground truth. Rows in review.needs_manual_review are the ones the annotator could not settle from the reference alone; the rest are confident readings, not verified facts.

interpretation_rules: Destination decides payment vs transfer: a person or organisation, or the speaker's own other account, is transfer even when the spoken verb is 'pay'; a merchant, biller or service is payment.

Money moved into the speaker's own wallet or account is deposit, even when the spoken verb is 'transfer'. This overlaps the schema's transfer definition and is the main call a reviewer may want to flip; it affects ivb_kn_017, ivb_kn_051, ivb_kn_060, ivb_kn_077, ivb_kn_079, ivb_hi_022, ivb_hi_055.
A capability or limit question is annotated with the intent of the action it asks about (for example 'what is my maximum withdrawal' is withdrawal), not as other.
Loan and insurance queries are other, as the schema specifies.

control_type is non-none only for dialogue or session control, or for stopping the action in progress. Cancelling or disabling a standing instruction (autopay, SIP deduction) is a banking operation, so control_type stays none and the request is described in notes.
For multi-request utterances the primary intent is the first request in utterance order; the rest go in notes. Where that choice also moves the amount, the row is flagged for review.

amount holds only the value tied to the primary intent. Thresholds ('alert below X') and intended transaction sizes ('enough for a X transaction') are recorded with a note. Fractions ('a quarter of it'), dates, times and durations are not amounts.

Identifier digits follow the schema: grouped numbers and 'double'/'triple' expand, leading letters and grammatical case suffixes stay in span but not in digits, and an ambiguous sequence sets digits to null and flags the row.
negation is positive unless an explicit negation bears on the request. Alternative questions ('has it come or not'), lexical failure words ('विफल', failed) and cancel verbs are not negation.
